note: A made-up example for tests and for showing the dashboard. The ideas, estimates and prior-work notes are invented; the arXiv papers are real but were picked by hand.

researcher.goal: One strong first-author result before applying for faculty jobs
researcher.setup: Dilution fridge with a scanning nanoSQUID; access to a shared stacking lab

ideas.title: Local thermal transport in magic-angle graphene
ideas.summary: Image heat flow near the magic angle with a nanoSQUID thermometer, to separate electronic and phonon contributions locally.

heilmeier.what: Map where heat is carried by electrons versus phonons in twisted bilayer graphene near 1.1 degrees.
heilmeier.today: Global thermal conductance measurements, averaged over twist-angle disorder.
heilmeier.who_cares: Groups arguing about strange-metal transport and Planckian dissipation.
heilmeier.risks: Thermometer sensitivity at the needed temperature; sample quality.
heilmeier.cost: Existing setup; two to three devices.
heilmeier.midterm: Thermal image of a single device at 1 K with domain contrast.
heilmeier.final: Temperature and density dependence of the local electronic share.

assumptions.text: The electronic contribution varies between twist-angle domains by more than the thermometer noise.
The nanoSQUID thermometer keeps its sensitivity in the field range needed.
We can make a device within 0.05 degrees of the magic angle.

queries: (abs:"magic-angle" OR abs:"twisted bilayer") AND abs:"thermal conductance"

closest.title: Magic angle in thermal conductivity of twisted bilayer graphene
closest.difference: Theory of the phonon part, not a local measurement.

cheapest_test.text: Image one existing device at 1 K for two weeks and look for domain contrast.

ideas.inversion: A calibrated local thermometer on a 2D device is a methods paper on its own.

ideas.title: Noise thermometry of an altermagnet thin film
ideas.summary: Use Johnson noise to look for the spin-split transport an altermagnet should show.

assumptions.text: Films with clean enough transport are available from a collaborator.
The spin-split signal is large enough to see in noise at our bandwidth.

cheapest_test.text: Estimate the signal from published band parameters before ordering films.

ideas.inversion: A noise setup for thin films is reusable for the next material.

ideas.title: Automated stacking with in-line twist-angle check
ideas.summary: Add Raman checks to the stacking workflow so bad stacks are caught before they are fabricated.

assumptions.text: Raman on the stamp predicts twist angle well enough to reject bad stacks.

ideas.inversion: Even if it fails, the lab gets a log of every stack.

ideas.title: Superconductivity in a new twisted trilayer stacking
ideas.summary: Look for superconductivity in a trilayer stacking no one has measured.

assumptions.text: This stacking has flat bands near charge neutrality.
We can control three twist angles at once.
Twist disorder is low enough over a device.

ideas.inversion: Transport on a new stacking is publishable even without superconductivity, at lower impact.

pi_questions: Would the lab support 12 months on the thermal project if the one-month test shows domain contrast?
Is the altermagnet film collaboration real enough to plan around?
